3.title: Adding Decimals
3.question: Use the standard algorithm: 4.89 + 8. Show your regrouping or division steps.
steps: Line up the decimal points. Add placeholder zeros so the numbers are 4.89 and 8.00.
Column 1 from the right: 9 + 0 = 9. Write 9.
Column 2 from the right: 8 + 0 = 8. Write 8.
Column 3 from the right: 4 + 8 = 12. Write 2 and carry 1 to the next column.
Write the final carried 1 in a new leftmost column.
Bring the decimal point straight down, keeping 2 decimal places: 12.89. The simplified decimal answer is 12.89.

4.title: Subtracting Decimals
4.question: Use the standard algorithm: 8.5 - 4.52. Show your regrouping or division steps.
steps: Line up the decimal points. Add placeholder zeros so the numbers are 8.50 and 4.52.
Column 1 from the right needs regrouping. Exchange one unit from a column to the left for ten units here, so this digit becomes 10.
Column 1 from the right: 10 − 2 = 8. Write 8.
Column 2 from the right needs regrouping. Exchange one unit from a column to the left for ten units here, so this digit becomes 14.
Column 2 from the right: 14 − 5 = 9. Write 9.
Column 3 from the right: 7 − 4 = 3. Write 3.
Bring the decimal point straight down, keeping 2 decimal places: 3.98. The simplified decimal answer is 3.98.

steps: Estimate the size first. Treat the factors as whole numbers: 4.5 becomes 45, and 5.5 becomes 55.
Multiply the whole numbers: 45 × 55 = 2475.
Count decimal places: 1 in 4.5 plus 1 in 5.5 gives 2.
Place the decimal point 2 places from the right in 2475, adding leading zeros if necessary: 24.75. Remove only unnecessary trailing zeros.

8.title: Dividing by Decimals
8.question: Use the standard algorithm: 11.52 ÷ 3.2. Show your regrouping or division steps.
steps: Make the divisor a whole number. Multiply BOTH numbers by 10: 11.52 ÷ 3.2 = 115.2 ÷ 32. This keeps the quotient unchanged.
32 goes into 115 3 times. Write 3; multiply 3 × 32 = 96; subtract 115 − 96 = 19.
Bring the decimal point straight up into the quotient before dividing the tenths.
Bring down the next digit, 2, to make 192. 32 goes into 192 6 times. Write 6; multiply 6 × 32 = 192; subtract 192 − 192 = 0.
Check using multiplication: 3.2 × 3.6 = 11.52. The quotient is 3.6.
